assumptions_made: Used synthetic data generation because the Hugging Face dataset doesn't provide suitable time series data for this experiment
Chose a seasonal period of 12 based on common monthly patterns in time series analysis
Used a simple linear trend combined with sine wave seasonal component for synthetic data
Applied a fixed 25% holdout for rolling evaluation as specified in design
Implemented naive persistence forecast as the baseline method
Used MAE as the primary metric for comparing forecast accuracy
The synthetic data generation creates realistic time series characteristics for meaningful experimentation

results.hypothesis: Test whether seasonal differencing improves one-step forecast error on a series with known seasonality.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Persistence forecast on the undifferenced series.
results.success_criteria: Seasonal differencing reduces one-step MAE by at least 10% against persistence.
results.notes: Without seasonal differencing MAE: 333.1260, With seasonal differencing MAE: 532.3417. Improvement: -59.80%.
results.methodological_validity: mixed real and synthetic inputs — findings are NOT interpretable as evidence; the synthetic inputs are listed in data_provenance.json
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
